topics.topic: Module and invoking actor for the pre-deployment OSV snapshot check
questions: Which module offers the operation that checks every installed distribution against the accepted OSV snapshot, and which actor invokes it before deployment?

quotes:
The image library decodes untrusted files. Before each deployment every distribution installed
   in the image is checked against a snapshot of the OSV database, ecosystem PyPI, that the deployment route accepts
   as current. That route owns the age limit, and no code of this service reads it. Any known vulnerability listed for an installed version
   blocks the deployment, whatever its severity, and a check that cannot complete does not pass.
   This is the policy the Client Portal already follows.
The check of rule 2 is built: it is the deployment route of this service, as it is the Client Portal's.
judgement.divergence: One implementer reuses the Client Portal deployment module and has the Portal deployment actor invoke it; another creates a separate deliverer deployment module invoked by a deliverer-specific deployment actor. The deployer notices different gate locations, configuration, and failure reporting.
judgement.why: The texts require and assign the check only to an unnamed deployment route, without naming a module capability or the actor that invokes it.

witness.initial: A deliverer image has been built with its resolved installed distributions and is awaiting deployment.
events: The deployment route checks every installed distribution against the accepted current OSV snapshot before deployment.
The deployment route either accepts the image or blocks it because a vulnerability is listed or the check cannot complete.
outcomes: The Client Portal's existing deployment module performs the check when the Portal deployment actor invokes it.
A separate deliverer deployment module performs the check when a deliverer-specific deployment actor invokes it.
witness.observer: The deployer locating and operating the vulnerability gate and receiving its failure report.
basis:

topics.topic: Owner and caller of scan, deliver, and record-publication flows
questions: Does the kernel itself execute the scan, deliver and record-publication calling flows, or does another owner-controlled flow call those operations while the kernel only provides reachability?

judgement.why: This asks the same question already decided by P4 about whether owner_delivery is the kernel calling flow or a separate service-side orchestration, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether owner_delivery is a defined kernel flow, external orchestration sketch, or absent/incomplete
quotes:
The calling agent is outside this service and organises the work (R0-15). It reads and publishes in the Portal with
its own session. It reaches the deliverer only through the routes of `module:deliverer_router`, which check the
token with `module:deliverer_api` and delegate to `module:photo_delivery`. The deliverer never calls the Portal. Showing a photo to the client is a later
action of the owner in the Portal and is not part of this flow.
precedent.why: State 4 defines owner_delivery as an externally executed calling-agent flow that composes the service routes and Portal operations, not as a deliverer-service capability.

topics.topic: Whether the R0-16 credential is the A5 bearer token or a separate credential
questions: Is this credential exactly the bearer token defined by A5, or is it an additional credential used between the kernel and the Portal front?
